vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: raai-knowledge-base-pro
Version: 3.5.1

The bundle is a comprehensive and professionally structured corporate knowledge management framework for Russian-speaking teams. Analysis of the shell scripts (install.sh, build.sh, and smoke-test.sh) reveals standard local file management and diagnostic logic with no evidence of remote payload execution, data exfiltration, or persistence mechanisms. The SKILL.md and associated markdown files provide detailed functional instructions for an AI agent to manage business processes (FAQs, SOPs, and onboarding) and do not contain malicious prompt injections or instructions to compromise sensitive environment variables.

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its stated KB/onboarding purpose, but there are small-but-important incoherences around declared network behavior and optional integrations (API keys / Telegram) and included install/test scripts — review these before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (knowledge base, onboarding, search, indexing) align with the files and config.yaml. Optional environment variables (OpenAI/Anthropic/Notion/Confluence/Google/Telegram) also make sense for the advertised integrations. The claim 'works without external SaaS' is defensible because config.yaml supports local storage, while external connectors are optional. Overall capability requests are proportionate to the described purpose, but the presence of many optional connector keys expands the attack surface if you enable them.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the user to fill config.yaml, run install.sh and smoke-test, index documents, and optionally connect remote storage and LLM APIs. Those actions require reading and uploading company documents to embedding/LLM providers when connectors are enabled. SKILL.md metadata reports network_behavior.makes_requests: false and uses_agent_telegram: false which contradicts the described Telegram bot, external indexing, and API-key options — this mismatch is noteworthy and should be clarified before use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no platform install spec (instruction-only), which reduces automatic risk. Included scripts (build.sh shown) perform benign packaging and smoke-test activities; build.sh contains no network downloads and uses only local shell utilities. install.sh and test/smoke-test.sh exist but their contents are not shown here — they should be inspected locally before execution. No downloads from arbitrary URLs were observed in the included build.sh.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required env vars are declared, but SKILL.md lists several optional API keys (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, NOTION_API_KEY, CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN, GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN). These map to supported integrations (embeddings/LLMs, remote KB sources, Telegram bot) and are therefore reasonable if you intend to enable those integrations. Because they are optional, the request for multiple credentials is not inherently disproportionate — but enabling them lets the skill access external services and your documents, so minimize privileges and scope when provisioning keys.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false; the skill is user-invocable and may be invoked autonomously (default), which is normal. There is no indication the skill requests permanent platform-level presence or modifies other skills' configs. The package contains install/test scripts that run locally only if you execute them; nothing indicates forced persistence beyond normal skill behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to be a coherent knowledge-base/onboarding product, but review these before installing:

- Clarify network behavior: SKILL.md metadata says it does not make network requests, yet the skill advertises optional integrations (OpenAI/Anthropic, Notion, Confluence, Google Drive, Telegram) that necessarily require outbound calls. Assume that connecting any of those will send data off your host.
- Inspect scripts locally: open install.sh and test/smoke-test.sh before running bash install.sh. build.sh is benign (packaging only), but an installer can modify your system — verify it does only what you expect.
- Principle of least privilege for credentials: if you enable integrations, create dedicated API keys/service accounts with minimal scopes (e.g., a Notion integration limited to a single workspace, Google service account with only Drive read access to specific folders, a Telegram bot token without extra privileges). Avoid using organization-wide admin keys.
- Data exfiltration risk: indexing will parse and (when configured) send documents to embedding/LLM providers. Decide whether sensitive documents should be indexed and whether your chosen provider's privacy policy is acceptable.
- Test in a sandbox: run the installer and the skill in an isolated environment with synthetic data first to confirm behavior and that logs/telemetry are acceptable.

If you want more assurance, provide the contents of install.sh and test/smoke-test.sh and I can check them line-by-line.
